Medical Quiz.question: ১) which amino acid is required for thyroid hormone synthesis?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Tyrosine is the amino acid required for the synthesis of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4). In thyroid follicular cells, tyrosine residues within thyroglobulin are iodinated by thyroid peroxidase, forming MIT (monoiodotyrosine) and DIT (diiodotyrosine). Coupling of these iodinated tyrosine residues produces T3 (MIT + DIT) and T4 (DIT + DIT). Iodine is also essential for thyroid hormone synthesis, but among the given amino acids, tyrosine is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Thyroid hormone synthesis requires tyrosine + iodine

  • MIT + DIT → T3

  • DIT + DIT → T4

  • Enzyme involved → thyroid peroxidase (TPO)

Exam Pearl:
Tyrosine is the amino acid backbone for synthesis of T3 and T4.

Medical Quiz.question: ২) which of the following is not a mechanisms for reducing blood glucose level by insulin?
Medical Quiz.option1: Increases transport and uptake of glucose by the cells
Medical Quiz.exp:
Insulin lowers blood glucose by increasing glucose uptake into cells, promoting glucose utilization, and inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis. It also stimulates glycogenesis (conversion of glucose to glycogen) in the liver and muscle, which helps reduce blood glucose levels. Therefore, inhibition of glycogenesis is not a mechanism of insulin action; rather, insulin promotes glycogen formation. Insulin also promotes lipogenesis and protein synthesis while inhibiting glycogenolysis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Insulin → ↑ glucose uptake

  • Insulin → ↑ glycogenesis

  • Insulin → ↓ gluconeogenesis

  • Insulin → ↓ glycogenolysis

Exam Pearl:
Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting glycogenesis, not by inhibiting it.

Medical Quiz.question: ৩) which one is secreted by parafollicular cell of thyroid gland?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The parafollicular cells (C cells) of the thyroid gland secrete calcitonin. Calcitonin helps regulate calcium homeostasis by decreasing serum calcium levels, mainly by inhibiting osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. In contrast, T3 and T4 are produced by the follicular cells of the thyroid gland, and rT3 is an inactive metabolite formed by peripheral conversion of thyroid hormones. Medullary thyroid carcinoma arises from parafollicular C cells and may produce excessive calcitonin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Parafollicular C cells → Calcitonin

  • Follicular cells → T3 and T4

  • Calcitonin → ↓ osteoclast activity → ↓ serum calcium

  • Medullary thyroid carcinoma → ↑ calcitonin

Exam Pearl:
C cells of thyroid = Calcitonin secretion.

Medical Quiz.question: ৪) The α and β subunits of insulin receptor are linked to each other by........?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The α and β subunits of the insulin receptor are linked together by disulfide bonds. The insulin receptor is a transmembrane receptor tyrosine kinase composed of two extracellular α subunits (insulin-binding domain) and two transmembrane β subunits (contain tyrosine kinase activity). These subunits are connected by disulfide linkages, maintaining the functional structure of the receptor. Binding of insulin to the α subunits activates the tyrosine kinase domain of the β subunits, leading to intracellular signaling and metabolic effects.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Insulin receptor → receptor tyrosine kinase

  • α subunit → extracellular insulin binding

  • β subunit → transmembrane + tyrosine kinase activity

  • α–β subunits linked by disulfide bonds

Exam Pearl:
Insulin receptor subunits are connected by disulfide bonds.

Medical Quiz.question: ৫) the process of transportation of iodine from follicular cells into the follicular cavity & bindiing with thyroglobulin is called....?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The process in which iodine binds to tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin within the thyroid follicular colloid is called organification. In this step, iodide is oxidized by thyroid peroxidase (TPO) and attached to thyroglobulin to form MIT (monoiodotyrosine) and DIT (diiodotyrosine). Iodide trapping refers to the active transport of iodide from blood into follicular cells by the sodium-iodide symporter. The coupling reaction is the next step where MIT and DIT combine to form T3 and T4.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Iodide trapping → blood → follicular cell

  • Organification → iodine + thyroglobulin tyrosine

  • MIT + DIT → T3

  • DIT + DIT → T4

  • Enzyme involved → thyroid peroxidase (TPO)

Exam Pearl:
Binding of iodine to thyroglobulin is called organification.

Medical Quiz.question: ৬) Somatostatin acts within islets of Langerhans and inhibits secretion of..... ?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Somatostatin is secreted by δ (delta) cells of the islets of Langerhans and acts locally (paracrine action) to inhibit the secretion of both insulin from β cells and glucagon from α cells. This helps regulate pancreatic endocrine activity and prevents excessive fluctuations in blood glucose levels. Somatostatin also inhibits gastrointestinal hormone secretion and slows gastrointestinal motility. Therefore, it has an inhibitory effect on both major pancreatic hormones.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • α cells → Glucagon

  • β cells → Insulin

  • δ cells → Somatostatin

  • Somatostatin → inhibits both insulin and glucagon

Exam Pearl:
Pancreatic somatostatin inhibits secretion of both insulin and gluca

Medical Quiz.question: ৭) Thyroxine cannot increases the metabolic activities all of the following body tissues except.........
Medical Quiz.exp:
Thyroxine (T4) increases metabolic activity in almost all tissues of the body, but it has little or no direct effect on the adult brain. The brain is relatively resistant to the metabolic effects of thyroid hormone after development is complete. In contrast, thyroxine significantly increases oxygen consumption, protein synthesis, and metabolic rate in tissues such as muscle, liver, heart, and spleen. Thyroid hormones are essential for normal brain development during fetal life and childhood, but their direct metabolic effect on mature brain tissue is limited.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Thyroxine → ↑ basal metabolic rate

  • Strong effects: heart, liver, skeletal muscle

  • Adult brain → minimal direct metabolic response

  • Thyroid hormone deficiency in childhood → impaired brain development

Exam Pearl:
Thyroxine increases metabolism of most tissues but has little effect on adult brain metabolic activity.

Medical Quiz.question: ৮) which one is the most active adrenal androgen?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The most active androgen among the given options is testosterone. Although the adrenal cortex secretes mainly weak androgens such as dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and androstenedione, these are converted in peripheral tissues into more potent androgens. Testosterone has significant androgenic activity and can be further converted to the more potent dihydrotestosterone (DHT) by 5α-reductase. Cortisol is a glucocorticoid and does not have androgenic activity.
Note: If the question specifically asks for the most active adrenal-derived androgen, DHEA/DHEA-S are the major adrenal products, but they are weak compared with testosterone.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Adrenal androgens: DHEA, DHEA-S, androstenedione

  • Most active androgen overall → DHT

  • Major active circulating androgen → Testosterone

  • Adrenal androgens are produced mainly by zona reticularis

Exam Pearl:
Testosterone is the most active androgen listed; ad

Medical Quiz.question: ৯) which is not true about effects of thyroid hormone in CVS?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Thyroid hormone increases cardiovascular activity by increasing heart rate, force of cardiac contraction, and cardiac output. It increases the expression of β1-adrenergic receptors in the heart, making the heart more responsive to catecholamines. Thyroid hormone also causes peripheral vasodilation due to increased tissue metabolism and heat production, reducing systemic vascular resistance. Therefore, vasoconstriction is not a true effect of thyroid hormone on the cardiovascular system. The increased cardiac output may cause a mild rise in systolic blood pressure.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Thyroid hormone → ↑ heart rate

  • Thyroid hormone → ↑ contractility

  • Thyroid hormone → ↑ cardiac output

  • Thyroid hormone → vasodilation (not vasoconstriction)

Exam Pearl:
Thyroid hormone increases cardiac activity but causes peripheral vasodilation.

Medical Quiz.question: ১০) failure of adrenal cortex to secrete corticosteroids is known as......?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Failure of the adrenal cortex to secrete corticosteroids (mainly cortisol and aldosterone) is known as Addison disease (primary adrenal insufficiency). It occurs due to destruction or dysfunction of the adrenal cortex, leading to deficiency of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids. Common features include fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. Cushing syndrome is due to excess cortisol secretion, while adrenogenital syndrome results from congenital adrenal enzyme defects causing excess androgen production.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Addison disease → ↓ cortisol + ↓ aldosterone

  • Primary adrenal insufficiency → ↑ ACTH → hyperpigmentation

  • Cushing syndrome → excess cortisol

  • Zona fasciculata → cortisol production

  • Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone production

Exam Pearl:
Adrenal cortex failure causing corticosteroid deficiency = Addison disease.

Medical Quiz.question: ১১) Hyperthyroidism in women leads to....?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Hyperthyroidism commonly causes menstrual disturbances due to disruption of the hypothalamic–pituitary–ovarian axis. In women, it most often leads to oligomenorrhea (infrequent menstruation) or amenorrhea due to altered gonadotropin secretion and increased metabolism of sex hormones. Hyperthyroidism may also cause lighter menstrual flow (hypomenorrhea). Menorrhagia is more commonly associated with hypothyroidism due to anovulation and coagulation abnormalities. Polymenorrhea and metrorrhagia are not typical menstrual manifestations of hyperthyroidism.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Hyperthyroidism → oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea

  • Hypothyroidism → menorrhagia

  • Thyroid hormones affect reproductive hormone regulation

  • Severe thyroid dysfunction may cause infertility

Exam Pearl:
Hyperthyroidism classically causes oligomenorrhea, while hypothyroidism causes menorrhagia.

Medical Quiz.question: ১২) which factor inhibits glucagon secretion?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Ketone bodies inhibit glucagon secretion by a negative feedback mechanism during fasting or prolonged starvation. When ketone levels rise, they reduce pancreatic α-cell activity, leading to decreased glucagon release. In contrast, gastrin and cholecystokinin (CCK) generally stimulate glucagon secretion, especially after meals. Cortisol tends to increase blood glucose by promoting gluconeogenesis and may enhance glucagon action rather than inhibit its secretion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Glucagon stimulators: amino acids, catecholamines, CCK, gastrin

  • Glucagon inhibitors: glucose, insulin, ketone bodies

  • α cells → glucagon

  • β cells → insulin

Exam Pearl:
Ketone bodies provide negative feedback and inhibit glucagon secretion.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৩) which is not true for Type II DM?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus usually develops gradually due to insulin resistance and progressive β-cell dysfunction. Symptoms often appear slowly and may remain unnoticed for years. Therefore, rapid onset of symptoms is not a typical feature of Type 2 DM and is more characteristic of Type 1 DM due to sudden insulin deficiency. Type 2 DM commonly occurs after 40 years of age, is associated with overweight/obesity, and involves impaired insulin receptor signaling causing insulin resistance (rather than complete absence of receptors).

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Type 2 DM → insulin resistance + relative insulin deficiency

  • Common age → >40 years

  • Common association → obesity/overweight

  • Onset → gradual

Exam Pearl:
Rapid onset of symptoms suggests Type 1 DM, not Type 2 DM.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৪) what is the location of thyroid hormone receptor?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The thyroid hormone receptor is located mainly in the nucleus. Thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) are lipid-soluble and enter cells by diffusion or transport proteins. T3 binds to nuclear thyroid hormone receptors (TRs), which are attached to thyroid hormone response elements on DNA. This hormone–receptor complex regulates gene transcription, leading to changes in protein synthesis and metabolic activity. Unlike peptide hormones, thyroid hormones do not act through cell membrane receptors.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Thyroid hormone receptor → nuclear receptor

  • Active hormone → T3

  • Mechanism → regulation of gene transcription

  • Steroid hormones → mainly intracellular receptors

Exam Pearl:
Thyroid hormone acts through nuclear receptors to alter gene expression.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৫) what is the chemical nature of the hormone TSH?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) is a glycoprotein hormone secreted by the anterior pituitary gland. It consists of α and β subunits; the α subunit is common with FSH, LH, and hCG, while the β subunit provides specificity for TSH action. TSH acts on thyroid follicular cells to stimulate synthesis and release of T3 and T4. Steroid hormones are derived from cholesterol, and tyrosine derivatives include thyroid hormones (T3/T4) and catecholamines, not TSH.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • TSH → glycoprotein hormone

  • Source → anterior pituitary

  • Acts on → thyroid follicular cells

  • Other glycoprotein hormones → FSH, LH, hCG

Exam Pearl:
TSH is a pituitary glycoprotein (protein) hormone.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৬) Hypothyroidism leads to......... in adults?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Hypothyroidism in adults leads to myxoedema, a condition caused by deficiency of thyroid hormones resulting in accumulation of mucopolysaccharides (glycosaminoglycans) in tissues. It presents with features such as fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, and slow metabolism. Cretinism occurs due to congenital hypothyroidism in infants and children, causing impaired physical and mental development. Goiter may occur in some causes of hypothyroidism, but it is not the defining adult manifestation. Exophthalmos is associated with Graves’ disease (hyperthyroidism).

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Adult hypothyroidism → Myxoedema

  • Childhood hypothyroidism → Cretinism

  • Graves’ disease → Exophthalmos

  • Hypothyroidism → ↓ metabolic rate

Exam Pearl:
Hypothyroidism in adults = myxoedema; in children = cretinism.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৭) which gland is called the ‘life-saving gland’?
Medical Quiz.exp:
The adrenal gland is called the “life-saving gland” because its hormones, especially cortisol and aldosterone, are essential for survival. Cortisol helps maintain blood pressure, glucose metabolism, and stress response, while aldosterone maintains sodium balance, fluid volume, and blood pressure. Complete failure of adrenal cortical function (Addison disease) can be fatal if untreated. The thyroid, parathyroid, and pancreas are important endocrine glands but are not classically termed life-saving glands.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Adrenal cortex → cortisol + aldosterone

  • Adrenal medulla → adrenaline + noradrenaline

  • Addison disease → life-threatening adrenal insufficiency

  • Aldosterone → maintains BP and electrolytes

Exam Pearl:
Adrenal gland is known as the “life-saving gland” because adrenal hormones are essential for survival.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৮) D cells or δ-cells of pancreas secretes........?
Medical Quiz.exp:
D (δ) cells of the pancreas are located in the islets of Langerhans and secrete somatostatin. Somatostatin acts locally within the pancreas to inhibit the secretion of both insulin from β cells and glucagon from α cells. Insulin is secreted by β cells, glucagon by α cells, and pancreatic polypeptide by PP (gamma/F) cells. Somatostatin also inhibits gastrointestinal hormone secretion and slows gastrointestinal motility.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • α cells → Glucagon

  • β cells → Insulin

  • δ cells → Somatostatin

  • PP/F cells → Pancreatic polypeptide

Exam Pearl:
Pancreatic δ-cells secrete somatostatin.

Medical Quiz.question: ১৯) Mineralocorticoids are transported in blood by binding with which plasma protein?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Mineralocorticoids (mainly aldosterone) are transported in blood primarily by binding to albumin. Unlike cortisol, which is mainly carried by corticosteroid-binding globulin (transcortin), aldosterone has a much lower affinity for plasma binding proteins and a significant proportion circulates in the free form. Albumin acts as the major carrier protein for aldosterone in plasma. Transferrin transports iron, and globulin is a general term that includes several binding proteins but is not the primary carrier for mineralocorticoids.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Aldosterone → mainly bound to albumin

  • Cortisol → bound to corticosteroid-binding globulin (CBG/transcortin)

  • Transferrin → iron transport

  • Free steroid fraction → biologically active

Exam Pearl:
Mineralocorticoids are transported mainly by albumin, unlike cortisol which binds CBG.

Medical Quiz.question: ২০) The α-chain of insulin contains how many amino acids?
Medical Quiz.exp:
Human insulin is composed of two polypeptide chains: α (A) chain and β (B) chain, linked by disulfide bonds. The α-chain contains 21 amino acids, while the β-chain contains 30 amino acids, making a total of 51 amino acids in the insulin molecule. Insulin is synthesized as preproinsulin, then processed to proinsulin and finally mature insulin after removal of the C-peptide.

High-Yield Rapid Recall

  • Insulin A (α) chain → 21 amino acids

  • Insulin B (β) chain → 30 amino acids

  • Total insulin amino acids → 51

  • A and B chains linked by disulfide bonds

Exam Pearl:
Insulin = A chain (21 aa) + B chain (30 aa) = 51 amino acids.
